sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐秘而伟大”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Picture with me, if you will, India during British colonial rule.
sentences.zh: 请跟我一起想象，英国殖民统治下的印度。

sentences.en: Let's say around the year 1865.
sentences.zh: 假设大约在1865年左右。

sentences.en: Picture a government office in Bombay, as the city was then known.
sentences.zh: 想象一下孟买的一个政府办公室，当时这座城市还被称为孟买。

sentences.en: Two British officers are discussing an uprising that has been challenging Britain's sovereignty over the subcontinent.
sentences.zh: 两名英国官员正在讨论一场一直在挑战英国对该次大陆主权的起义。

sentences.en: It's May, the hottest month in India.
sentences.zh: 正值五月，印度最热的月份。

sentences.en: Temperatures have soared to over 100 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 气温飙升至华氏100度以上。

sentences.en: The officers are sweating.
sentences.zh: 官员们汗流浃背。

sentences.en: There's no air conditioning, of course, but they have a servant who brings them two ice-cold drinks.
sentences.zh: 当然没有空调，但他们有一个仆人给他们送来两杯冰镇饮料。

sentences.en: The officers take sips of their drinks and swirl the ice in their glasses.
sentences.zh: 官员们啜饮着饮料，在杯子里转动着冰块。

sentences.en: And at this moment, these cold drinks, dripping with condensation, feel like a small miracle to these colonialist wankers.
sentences.zh: 就在这一刻，这些挂着凝结水珠的冰饮，对这群殖民主义混蛋来说就像是个小小的奇迹。

sentences.en: But actually, the ice was a kind of miracle.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这冰块本身就是一种奇迹。

sentences.en: That's our own little miracle, Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: 那是我们自己的小奇迹，萨姆·格林斯潘。

sentences.en: Because in 1865, no one had refrigerators.
sentences.zh: 因为在1865年，没有人有冰箱。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be for another half century until they started appearing in the U.S., let alone India.
sentences.zh: 还要再过半个世纪冰箱才开始在美国出现，更不用说印度了。

sentences.en: Think about the ice in those officers' glasses.
sentences.zh: 想想那些官员杯子里的冰。

sentences.en: If you were to zoom out from those glasses, and out, and out, and then zoom in on the United States, on Boston, on a frozen lake in the dead of winter,
sentences.zh: 如果你从这些杯子开始，不断往外拉远，再拉远，然后聚焦到美国，聚焦到波士顿，聚焦到深冬时节的一座冰冻的湖泊上，

sentences.en: there, you'd find men working.
sentences.zh: 在那里，你会发现人们在工作。

sentences.en: You see a lot of men and horses and a lot of activity going on.
sentences.zh: 你会看到很多人、马匹以及一片热火朝天的景象。

sentences.en: And then you'll see horse-drawn plows, pikes and pusher bars or poles.
sentences.zh: 然后你会看到马拉犁、冰钩和推杆或撑竿。

sentences.en: That's Rick Smith, amateur historian of the American ice trade.
sentences.zh: 那是里克·史密斯，美国冰品贸易的业余历史学家。

sentences.en: So all of these people together were on the lake harvesting ice.
sentences.zh: 所以所有人聚集在湖上采冰。

sentences.en: Workers would cut ice out of a frozen pond, haul it to port, put it on a ship, and send it on a four-month journey to India.
sentences.zh: 工人们从冻结的池塘里切割冰块，将其运到港口，装上船，然后送往印度，展开为期四个月的航程。

sentences.en: Any ice that British officers in colonial India would have had in their drinks would have started out on the top of a pond in Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 殖民地印度的英国官员杯子里的任何冰块，最初都来自马萨诸塞州一个池塘的表面。

sentences.en: The tools of the ice trade varied by location, but generally it went like this.
sentences.zh: 冰品贸易的工具因地而异，但大致过程是这样的。

sentences.en: So the first step is to measure the ice.
sentences.zh: 所以第一步是测量冰的厚度。

sentences.en: There's a small drill hole that's drilled in and a measurement taken of how thick the ice is because it had to be at least 14 inches thick.
sentences.zh: 在一个钻出的小孔里测量冰有多厚，因为冰必须至少有14英寸厚。

sentences.en: 14 inches of ice was thick enough to hold the team of workers and horses that would be assembled,
sentences.zh: 14英寸厚的冰足以承载即将组建的工人和马匹队伍，

sentences.en: starting usually the day after Christmas.
sentences.zh: 通常从圣诞节的第二天开始。

sentences.en: The workers would come out onto the ice, clear off snow and debris, and then...
sentences.zh: 工人们会走到冰面上，清除积雪和杂物，然后……

sentences.en: The horse-drawn ice plows would start to score the ice.
sentences.zh: 马拉冰犁开始在冰面上划线。

sentences.en: And they would do this all over the ice until they had made a grid.
sentences.zh: 他们会在整个冰面上这样做，直到划出一个网格。

sentences.en: A grid on the ice.
sentences.zh: 冰面上的一个网格。

sentences.en: They kind of make a checkerboard, let's say.
sentences.zh: 比方说，他们有点像在做棋盘。

sentences.en: Workers would use giant hand saws and ice pikes, basically big sticks with sharp ends,
sentences.zh: 工人们会使用巨大的手锯和冰钩，基本上就是带尖头的大棍子，

sentences.en: to break up the squares of ice so that they were floating in the water.
sentences.zh: 把方块冰切开，让它们浮在水面上。

sentences.en: A steam-powered conveyor belt would haul these cakes of ice out of the water,
sentences.zh: 蒸汽驱动的传送带会把这些冰块从水中拉出来，

sentences.en: and they would go through a planer, so each cake would become smooth and uniform.
sentences.zh: 它们会通过一台刨冰机，这样每块冰都会变得光滑且大小一致。

sentences.en: Then they'd be stacked in a nearby ice house, a large wooden structure that would hold tons of ice.
sentences.zh: 然后它们会被堆放在附近的冰库里，这是一个能容纳数吨冰的大型木质建筑。

sentences.en: Ice houses often had a railroad siding, so the ice could be loaded up onto a train and freighted off to the city.
sentences.zh: 冰库通常有铁路支线，这样冰块就可以装上火车运往城市。

sentences.en: If you've seen the Disney movie Frozen, the ice harvesting scene is actually pretty accurate.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过迪士尼电影《冰雪奇缘》，里面的采冰场景其实相当准确。

sentences.en: At its peak, ice harvesting happened on lakes all over New England, New York, Michigan,
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期，新英格兰、纽约、密歇根各地的湖泊都在进行采冰，

sentences.en: in the Poconos region of northeastern Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 还有宾夕法尼亚州东北部的波科诺山地区。

sentences.en: It was, at one time, the major industry.
sentences.zh: 它曾经是一个主要的产业。

sentences.en: My father actually worked on the ice harvesting back in the 1930s and 40s and even into the 50s.
sentences.zh: 我父亲实际上在20世纪30、40年代甚至50年代都从事过采冰工作。

sentences.en: This entire area of the Poconos, that was pretty much the only thing that you could do in the wintertime for work.
sentences.zh: 波科诺的整个这一带，这几乎是你在冬天唯一能找到的工作。

sentences.en: But now, it's gone.
sentences.zh: 但现在，它没了。

sentences.en: It just disappeared entirely.
sentences.zh: 它完全消失了。

sentences.en: It's a bit sad, in a way, that an industry melted away, as it were.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，一个产业就这样融化了，这让人有点难过。

sentences.en: Here to also remember the natural ice industry is Gavin Waitman.
sentences.zh: 同样来缅怀天然冰产业的有加文·韦特曼。

sentences.en: I'm Gavin Waitman.
sentences.zh: 我是加文·韦特曼。

sentences.en: I live in London, and I write social history books, mainly.
sentences.zh: 我住在伦敦，主要撰写社会历史书籍。

sentences.en: And one of my most successful books was called The Frozen Water Trade.
sentences.zh: 我最成功的一本书叫《冷冻水贸易》。

sentences.en: One edition of the book is actually titled The Frozen Water Trade, A True Story.
sentences.zh: 该书的一个版本实际上名为《冷冻水贸易：真实的故事》。

sentences.en: Maybe because even Gavin's publishers thought the prospect of cutting frozen water out of American lakes
sentences.zh: 也许是因为连加文的出版商都觉得，从美国湖泊中切割冷冻水

sentences.en: and shipping it overseas sounded made up.
sentences.zh: 并将其运到海外的想法听起来像是虚构的。

sentences.en: But that is exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 但那确实发生了。

sentences.en: Ice was being harvested from all over the American northeast,
sentences.zh: 冰块从美国东北部各地被采收，

sentences.en: packed onto railroad cars and ships,
sentences.zh: 打包进火车车厢和船只，

sentences.en: and sent out to the southern U.S., the Caribbean, and British colonists in India.
sentences.zh: 运往美国南部、加勒比地区以及印度的英国殖民者手中。

sentences.en: The development of the international ice trade can be traced back to one person,
sentences.zh: 国际冰品贸易的发展可以追溯到一个人，

sentences.en: a man who, by the end of his life, would come to be known as the Ice King,
sentences.zh: 一个到他生命的尽头被称为“冰王”的人，

sentences.en: a guy named Frederick Tudor.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫弗雷德里克·都铎的家伙。

sentences.en: He was the son of a moderately well-off Boston family.
sentences.zh: 他是波士顿一个家境中等偏上的家庭的儿子。

sentences.en: I think he'd be a very odd bloke.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他会是个非常古怪的家伙。

sentences.en: Sorry, I shouldn't use the word bloke.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我不应该用“家伙”这个词。

sentences.en: It's an English term.
sentences.zh: 这是一个英国词汇。

sentences.en: To meet him, I think he'd be a pretty eccentric bloke.
sentences.zh: 去见他的时候，我觉得他会是个相当古怪的家伙。

sentences.en: Now, Tudor did not invent the idea of moving frozen water from one place to another.
sentences.zh: 现在，都铎并不是第一个萌生将冷冻水从一个地方运到另一个地方的人。

sentences.en: The practice actually began in Europe and South America, well before Tudor's time.
sentences.zh: 这种做法实际上在都铎之前很久就在欧洲和南美开始了。

sentences.en: People would go up to the mountains and bring down ice and snow.
sentences.zh: 人们会去山上把冰雪带下来。

sentences.en: Although Tudor might not have known about this,
sentences.zh: 虽然都铎可能并不知道这一点，

sentences.en: but he did know that New Englanders had a local tradition of cutting ice out of local lakes
sentences.zh: 但他确实知道新英格兰人有一个当地的传统，即从当地湖泊中切冰

sentences.en: and using it to keep food cool.
sentences.zh: 并用它来给食物保鲜。

sentences.en: When Frederick Tudor was a young man, farmers certainly did keep ice,
sentences.zh: 当弗雷德里克·都铎还是个年轻人的时候，农民们确实会保存冰，

sentences.en: which they collected in the winter,
sentences.zh: 那是他们在冬天收集的，

sentences.en: and then when they were taking, say, butter to market in the summer,
sentences.zh: 然后当他们在夏天把黄油等东西运到市场出售时，

sentences.en: they would take a bit of this ice in order to prevent it from melting.
sentences.zh: 他们会带上一小块冰以防止黄油融化。

sentences.en: So it was used on a small scale in that way,
sentences.zh: 所以它当时是以这种小规模的方式使用的，

sentences.en: but it wasn't put into drinks and that sort of thing,
sentences.zh: 但并没有被放进饮料之类的地方，

sentences.en: and it was very localized.
sentences.zh: 而且非常本土化。

sentences.en: When Tudor was in his early 20s,
sentences.zh: 当都铎二十出头时，

sentences.en: he and his brother William took a trip to the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 他和他的兄弟威廉去加勒比地区旅行了一趟。

sentences.en: And he thought, these people need ice.
sentences.zh: 他想，这些人需要冰。

sentences.en: Tudor's idea was that he was going to make his fortune
sentences.zh: 都铎的想法是，他要发财了，

sentences.en: because ice was a frozen asset of New England.
sentences.zh: 因为冰是新英格兰的一种冷冻资产。

sentences.en: It wasn't being used, and he felt he could sell it,
sentences.zh: 它没有被利用起来，他觉得他可以把它卖出去，

sentences.en: particularly to countries which were very hot and could have no ice
sentences.zh: 特别是卖给那些非常炎热且根本没有冰的国家，

sentences.en: unless he delivered it to them from Boston lakes and ponds.
sentences.zh: 除非他把冰从波士顿的湖泊和池塘运送给他们。

sentences.en: And Bostonians thought he was absolutely crazy.
sentences.zh: 波士顿人觉得他简直疯了。

sentences.en: But Tudor was convinced that this could work.
sentences.zh: 但都铎坚信这行得通。

sentences.en: Cocky, even.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说是傲慢。

sentences.en: He wrote that selling ice would make him, quote,
sentences.zh: 他写道，卖冰会让他，引用原话，

sentences.en: inevitably and unavoidably rich.
sentences.zh: 不可避免、无法抗拒地变得富有。

sentences.en: Tudor set up shop on the banks of a pond called Fresh Pond
sentences.zh: 都铎在马萨诸塞州剑桥市一个名为“新鲜池塘”的湖岸边

sentences.en: in Cambridge, Massachusetts,
sentences.zh: 建立了自己的基地，

sentences.en: just about two miles northwest of Harvard Square.
sentences.zh: 就在哈佛广场西北约两英里处。

sentences.en: And after he learned how to get ice out of the lake,
sentences.zh: 在学会了如何把冰从湖里取出来之后，

sentences.en: Tudor started looking for new ways to keep ice frozen.
sentences.zh: 都铎开始寻找保持冰不融化的新方法。

sentences.en: Frederick Tudor experimented with all sorts of insulating materials,
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·都铎试验了各种绝缘材料，

sentences.en: because remember, this was more than 100 years
sentences.zh: 因为记住，这比冰箱开始出现在人们家中

sentences.en: before refrigerators began appearing in people's houses.
sentences.zh: 早了100多年。

sentences.en: He discovered that sawdust was a remarkably good insulator,
sentences.zh: 他发现木屑是一种非常好的绝缘体，

sentences.en: and he could get it for next to nothing from lumber mills in Maine.
sentences.zh: 他可以从缅因州的木材厂几乎不花钱地弄到木屑。

sentences.en: Kept inside of a dry ice house and packed with sawdust,
sentences.zh: 放在干燥的冰库里并用木屑压实，

sentences.en: Tudor would eventually discover that he could keep ice stable for years.
sentences.zh: 都铎最终发现他可以让冰块保持稳定数年之久。

sentences.en: So all Tudor had to do was get the ice onto a ship and send it to hotter climates.
sentences.zh: 所以都铎要做的就是把冰搬上船，送到更热的气候区。

sentences.en: His first attempt to sell ice outside Boston was made with a little shipment to Martinique.
sentences.zh: 他第一次尝试在波士顿以外的地方卖冰，是通过向马提尼克岛运送的一小批货。

sentences.en: Shippers didn't want to ship ice.
sentences.zh: 船运公司不想运冰。

sentences.en: It seemed the most ridiculous cargo.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是最荒谬的货物。

sentences.en: So he fitted out a ship himself.
sentences.zh: 于是他自己改装了一艘船。

sentences.en: The ice made it to the Caribbean no problem,
sentences.zh: 冰顺利到达了加勒比地区，

sentences.en: but Martinique was not equipped to deal with a temperature-sensitive product
sentences.zh: 但马提尼克岛没有配备处理这种对温度敏感的产品的设施，

sentences.en: that literally melts into something worthless without the right infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 如果没有合适的基建设施，这种产品字面意思上会融化成毫无价值的东西。

sentences.en: It was a bit of a failure, really, because when it got to Martinique,
sentences.zh: 这其实有点失败，因为当冰到达马提尼克岛时，

sentences.en: no one knew how to keep ice.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道该怎么保存冰。

sentences.en: He wrote a rather amusing entry in his diary about the fact that people
sentences.zh: 他在日记中写了一段相当有趣的记录，关于人们

sentences.en: wrapped their piece of ice in blankets and wandered off
sentences.zh: 把他们的冰块用毯子包裹起来，然后到处走，

sentences.en: and wondered why it had disappeared when they got home.
sentences.zh: 并纳闷为什么他们回到家时冰块已经消失了。

sentences.en: The newspapers ridiculed Tudor.
sentences.zh: 报纸嘲笑了都铎。

sentences.en: But Tudor would not be discouraged.
sentences.zh: 但都铎没有气馁。

sentences.en: He went back to the Caribbean and to the southern United States
sentences.zh: 他又回到了加勒比地区和美国南部，

sentences.en: and showed people there how to build more effective ice houses.
sentences.zh: 并向当地人展示了如何建造更有效的冰库。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 这成功了。

sentences.en: Frozen water carved out of lakes and ponds
sentences.zh: 从湖泊和池塘中切下来的冷冻水

sentences.en: was being transported hundreds to thousands of miles.
sentences.zh: 正被运送到数白甚至数千英里之外。

sentences.en: He had a rough time getting it going.
sentences.zh: 他一开始过得很艰难。

sentences.en: He went bankrupt a couple of times, but he did manage it in the end.
sentences.zh: 他破产了好几次，但最终还是成功了。

sentences.en: But for all of Tudor's innovation in insulation and supply chain logistics,
sentences.zh: 但尽管都铎在绝缘和供应链物流方面有种种创新，

sentences.en: his true genius was as a marketer.
sentences.zh: 他真正的天才之处在于他是一名营销大师。

sentences.en: Before Tudor, ice had mostly just been used to preserve foodstuffs.
sentences.zh: 在都铎之前，冰大多只用来保存食品。

sentences.en: Frederick Tudor pioneered the radical idea of putting ice into beverages.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·都铎开创了把冰放进饮料中的激进想法。

sentences.en: When you first drink a cold drink like that, when you're not used to it,
sentences.zh: 当你第一次喝这种冰饮时，如果你不习惯，

sentences.en: it's quite a shock, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实会感到相当震撼。

sentences.en: So he had to persuade people that what he was selling was a luxury and worth paying for.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须说服人们，他卖的东西是奢侈品，并且物有所值。

sentences.en: Tudor would tout his ice around to bars and so on, offer it for free, say, look, try this, try that.
sentences.zh: 都铎会向酒吧等地兜售他的冰，免费送给他们，说，看，试试这个，试试那个。

sentences.en: He had to persuade people that what he was selling was going to improve their lives, if you like.
sentences.zh: 他必须说服人们，他卖的东西会改善他们的生活，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: It wasn't self-evident to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他（指当地人）来说并不是显而易见的。

sentences.en: The first one, as they say, is always free.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所说，第一杯总是免费的。

sentences.en: Tudor wrote,
sentences.zh: 都铎写道，

sentences.en: once people had tried chilled drinks, they were hooked and would no longer tolerate tepid water.
sentences.zh: 一旦人们尝试了冰镇饮料，他们就上瘾了，再也无法忍受温水。

sentences.en: He was a bit like a sort of drug pusher.
sentences.zh: 他有点像某种贩毒者。

sentences.en: And like any drug pusher, Tudor soon found himself with a lot of competition.
sentences.zh: 和任何贩毒者一样，都铎很快发现自己面临着激烈的竞争。

sentences.en: Rival ice companies set up shop on Tudor's fresh pond and staked a claim to it.
sentences.zh: 竞争对手的冰品公司在都铎的新鲜池塘开张并宣称拥有该处的主权。

sentences.en: In fact, they had to go get a Harvard professor to devise a map carving up boundaries for the ice rights of different parties all on the same lake.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们不得不找来一位哈佛教授来绘制一张地图，划分出在同一个湖上不同各方的采冰权边界。

sentences.en: And of course, it wasn't just fresh pond, because now any body of water that was frozen thick enough to support the weight of an ice harvesting crew was a hot commodity.
sentences.zh: 当然，不仅仅是新鲜池塘，因为现在任何冻得足够厚、足以承受采冰队重量的水体都是抢手货。

sentences.en: Ice began to get harvested all over New England and New York, Pennsylvania, and Canada.
sentences.zh: 新英格兰、纽约、宾夕法尼亚和加拿大的各地都开始采冰。

sentences.en: One of Tudor's competitors, the Wenham Lake Ice Company, based out of Wenham Lake, about 30 miles north of Boston,
sentences.zh: 都铎的一个竞争对手——温纳姆湖冰业公司，总部设在波士顿以北约30英里处的温纳姆湖，

sentences.en: somehow they managed to persuade their buyers that their ice was premium product.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，他们成功地说服了买家，证明他们的冰是优质产品。

sentences.en: Ice from Wenham Lake would be sold as especially pure.
sentences.zh: 温汉姆湖的冰会被作为特别纯净的冰出售。

sentences.en: It was nonsense, really, but it was a way of marketing.
sentences.zh: 这其实是无稽之谈，但也是一种营销手段。

sentences.en: You know, our ice is better than yours.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们的冰比你们的好。

sentences.en: Legend has it that Queen Victoria would only use Wenham Lake ice.
sentences.zh: 传说维多利亚女王只用温汉姆湖的冰。

sentences.en: And maybe you're thinking, why would England need to import ice all the way from North America when there are plenty of really cold places that are closer?
sentences.zh: 也许你在想，既然有很多离得更近的真正寒冷的地方，英国为什么还要一路从北美进口冰呢？

sentences.en: Norway wondered the same thing.
sentences.zh: 挪威人也有同样的疑问。

sentences.en: Norwegian businessmen tried breaking into the ice biz, even going so far as to rename one of their lakes Wenham Lake,
sentences.zh: 挪威商人试图打入冰块生意，甚至将他们的一座湖改名为温汉姆湖，

sentences.en: in an attempt to profit from the Wenham Lake Ice Company's prestige and name recognition.
sentences.zh: 以此来借用温汉姆湖冰业公司的声誉和知名度获利。

sentences.en: Frederick Tudor's company never made a play for the UK ice market,
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·蒂铎的公司从未涉足英国冰市，

sentences.en: which turned out to be a pretty good business move, because ice never really took off in England.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这是一步相当不错的商业棋，因为冰在英国从未真正流行起来。

sentences.en: Even in the 20th century, American GIs in England were shocked to find nothing but warm beer.
sentences.zh: 甚至在20世纪，英国的美国大兵惊讶地发现除了温啤酒什么也没有。

sentences.en: And there were several in the Air Force who said they would put their drinks in the back of a plane
sentences.zh: 空军里有好几个人说，他们会把饮料放在飞机后舱，

sentences.en: and fly it to about 25,000 feet, where it would chill.
sentences.zh: 然后把它飞到大约25,000英尺的高空去冷藏。

sentences.en: Chill a little bit, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少能稍微冰镇一下。

sentences.en: But there's one place where Brits could not get enough ice.
sentences.zh: 但有一个地方，英国人对冰的需求怎么也满足不了。

sentences.en: India.
sentences.zh: 印度。

sentences.en: So this is three months in the hold of a ship, twice across the equator.
sentences.zh: 所以在船舱里要待上三个月，两次穿过赤道。

sentences.en: So it was quite a remarkable survival rate for the ice,
sentences.zh: 所以冰的存活率相当惊人，

sentences.en: which was eventually unloaded in Bombay, as it was called then, Madras and Calcutta.
sentences.zh: 最终在当时的孟买、马德拉斯和加尔各答卸货。

sentences.en: Despite all this, Frederick Tudor never really became inevitably and unavoidably rich, like he'd predicted.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，弗雷德里克·蒂铎并没有像他预测的那样变得不可避免地大发横财。

sentences.en: His whole life, he was in and out of debt and debtor's prisons.
sentences.zh: 他的一生都在负债和债务人监狱之间度过。

sentences.en: And he eventually became not particularly wealthy, but well enough of.
sentences.zh: 他最终没有变得特别富有，但也算得上衣食无忧。

sentences.en: And he bought an estate outside Boston and lived a kind of rural life.
sentences.zh: 他在波士顿郊外买了一处房产，过着一种乡村生活。

sentences.en: But still, it wouldn't be until 40 years after Tudor's death, squarely in the 20th century, that the natural ice industry began to shift.
sentences.zh: 不过，直到蒂铎死后40年，正值20世纪，天然冰产业才开始发生转变。

sentences.en: The earliest refrigerators started appearing in the 19-teens, but the early models broke all the time.
sentences.zh: 最早的电冰箱出现在1910年代，但早期型号总是坏。

sentences.en: The physics of cooling proved much harder to master than heating.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，制冷物理学比供暖要难掌握得多。

sentences.en: And of course, you had to have electricity, which most homes in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当然，你还得有电，而美国大多数家庭

sentences.en: didn't have until the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪20年代才有电。

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, the technology kept improving and consumers began to have a choice of getting natural ice scraped off the top of a frozen pond
sentences.zh: 技术稳步而持续地改进，消费者开始有了选择：是用从结冰池塘表面刮下来的天然冰，

sentences.en: or ice made in a factory where the water could be better controlled and filtered, which started to get more important because...
sentences.zh: 还是用工厂制造的冰，那里的水可以得到更好的控制和过滤，这变得越来越重要，因为……

sentences.en: As the towns grew, as buildings grew up around Fresh Pond and the other lakes that were used for supply, sewage would get into them.
sentences.zh: 随着城镇的扩大，随着弗雷ッシュ池塘（Fresh Pond）及其他用作水源的湖泊周围建起高楼，污水会流入其中。

sentences.en: It became a health hazard.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种健康危害。

sentences.en: And this became a great problem for the natural ice industry.
sentences.zh: 这对天然冰产业来说成了一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And to make matters worse for the natural ice trade, the Northeast experienced a spate of unusually warm winters.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，美国东北部经历了一连串异常温暖的冬天，这对天然冰贸易无异于雪上加霜。

sentences.en: The ponds that had been supplying the world's ice weren't freezing as well.
sentences.zh: 一直为世界供应冰块的池塘结冰情况不佳。

sentences.en: The newspapers were calling it an ice famine.
sentences.zh: 报纸称之为“冰荒”。

sentences.en: The supply region shifted northward, towards Maine, where the climate was colder and the water less polluted.
sentences.zh: 供应区向北转移到了缅因州，那里的气候更冷，水污染更少。

sentences.en: But by then, the writing was on the wall.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，大势已去。

sentences.en: The natural ice trade was on its way out in the 1920s, but hung on in some places, especially rural places, until as late as the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 天然冰贸易在20世纪20年代走向消亡，但在某些地方，尤其是乡村地区，一直坚持到了20世纪50年代。

sentences.en: And ice harvests still happen in some places.
sentences.zh: 而且某些地方仍然在进行采冰。

sentences.en: There's a renewed interest in the tradition.
sentences.zh: 人们对这项传统重新燃起了兴趣。

sentences.en: In Pennsylvania and all over New England, there are some ice harvest revivals.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州和整个新英格兰，有一些采冰复兴活动。

sentences.en: But, you know, with some updated tools, and it's all more for heritage value.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，用了一些更新的工具，这更多是为了文化遗产的价值。

sentences.en: It's not like people are still putting frozen pond water in their drinks.
sentences.zh: 并不是说人们还在把冻池塘的水放进饮料里。

sentences.en: But as for the actual site where all of this started, Fresh Pond in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the ice trade might as well have never existed.
sentences.zh: 但至于这一切开始的实际地点——马萨诸塞州剑桥市的弗雷什池塘，这里的冰贸易简直就像从未存在过一样。

sentences.en: When I was researching this story, I stayed up in Cambridge, and I went out to Fresh Pond.
sentences.zh: 当我研究这个故事时，我住在剑桥，然后去了弗雷什池塘。

sentences.en: People were jogging around the lake, and they were confronted by me, this completely mad Englishman, saying,
sentences.zh: 人们绕着湖慢跑，然后他们遇到了我这个完全疯狂的英国人，我说：

sentences.en: Excuse me, do you know that this ice used to be transported to India from this pond?
sentences.zh: “打扰一下，你知道以前这里的冰是从这个池塘运到印度的吗？”

sentences.en: And they looked at me as if I was completely mad.
sentences.zh: 他们看着我，就像看着一个疯子一样。

sentences.en: So at Fresh Pond, there's no plaque or anything?
sentences.zh: 所以在弗雷什池塘，连个牌匾都没有吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Cambridge, Massachusetts has finally found something to not commemorate with a plaque.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州剑桥市终于找到了一个不用立牌匾纪念的事物。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sam Greenspan with Katie Mingle, Avery Truffman,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由山姆·格林斯潘与凯蒂·明格、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼制作，

sentences.en: Kurt Colstead, Delaney Hall, Sharif Youssef, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 还有库尔特·科尔斯特德、德莱尼·霍尔、谢里夫·优素福以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Rosie Weinberg, Stein Ivar Luteida, and Dylan Garrett-Smith, who reached out to us about this story.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢罗西·温伯格、斯坦·伊瓦尔·卢泰达和迪伦·加勒特-史密斯，他们就这个故事联系了我们。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，制作于加利福尼亚州美丽奥克兰市中心的一家建筑与室内设计公司 ArcSign 的办公室。

sentences.zh: 你可以在 Facebook 上找到并点赞本节目。

sentences.en: The show's Twitter is at 99PI.org, and my Twitter is at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 节目的 Twitter 是 @99PI.org，我的 Twitter 是 @Roman Mars。

sentences.en: Make sure you tag me if you have a picture of a coin that you'd like to share.
sentences.zh: 如果你有想分享的硬币照片，一定要艾特我。

sentences.en: We're all on Instagram, Tumblr, and Spotify, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram、Tumblr 和 Spotify 上。

sentences.en: But this week, your mission is to spend some quality time with the new, beautiful 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 但本周你的任务是花点时间好好体验一下全新、美丽的 99PI.org。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: 审慎电台。
